trust_decision.summary: URL(scope=...) concatenates the raw client Host header with scope['path'] and re-parses with urlsplit, so the derived request.url.path is decided by attacker bytes rather than by scope['path']; the fix only accepts a Host matching a hostname/IP[:port] regex.

landing_point.why: Summary names Host header and request.url.path; URL.__init__ is the only place the Host header is joined into the URL string.

fix_sites.entry_point: Request.url / HTTPConnection.url (starlette/requests.py:110-113) and public URL(scope=...) constructor

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: All URL-from-scope consumers (requests.py:112, requests.py:129, routing.py:705, staticfiles.py:142, middleware/httpsredirect.py:12, middleware/trustedhost.py:55) go through the single fixed constructor.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: For the O8 path-differential route: 'the advisory is about the Host header; a percent-encoded ?/# in the path is the server's decoding, not Host validation'.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Legitimate Host values with port, IPv6 literals ([::1]:8000), uppercase and trailing-dot names must still populate request.url netloc and absolute url_for/redirect URLs; rejecting or 400-ing on Host breaks TrustedHost www-redirect, HTTPS redirect and url_for.

O8_uncovered_routes.route: scope['path'] containing decoded '?' or '#' (from %3F/%23) is appended unescaped at datastructures.py:52/59/61 and urlsplit truncates url.path, so request.url.path still differs from scope['path'] after the fix.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Not the Host header; the fix comment talks only about Host chars, and a truncated path is a prefix of the real one so many prefix checks still hold.

O8_uncovered_routes.route: No Host header and no server tuple: url = path, so a scope path beginning '//' is parsed by urlsplit as a netloc and url.path differs from scope['path'].
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Unusual server configuration (no server in scope); fix also falls back here for a rejected Host when server is None.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a second base_url/url builder that formats Host directly instead of calling URL(scope=...)
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: base_url already rebuilds a scope copy; a maintainer optimising it could inline the f-string.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Host route matcher using split(':')[0] on raw Host, a separator-split differential with the URL parser
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Already a hand-rolled parse of Host; a planted variant deriving path params from it is plausible.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: TrustedHost uses its own split(':')[0] parse, different from the regex in the fix
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Two Host parsers already exist and disagree; adding a path-based middleware that uses url.path here is natural.

O9_family: parser differential: Host header joined into URL string and re-parsed (CWE-444/CWE-1289)

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Strip/escape only '/' or '?' from the Host header (or reject with 400) instead of validating the full host[:port]/IPv6 shape, leaving '@', '#', backslash and the path-side '?'/'#' differential.

out_of_scope_notes: starlette/middleware/wsgi.py:58-71 copies Host into HTTP_HOST for WSGI apps unvalidated; that is the wrapped app's URL reconstruction, not request.url.
TrustedHost www-redirect builds the redirect from URL(scope) netloc (starlette/middleware/trustedhost.py:55-56); open-redirect concerns are out of scope.
unverified: O8 route 1 assumes ASGI servers put percent-decoded '?'/'#' into scope['path'] (ASGI spec says path is decoded); not checked against a server here.
Whether either O8 route still exists in the latest release: no latest code supplied.
